dedupe_keys.name: midas modular ice cream factory dataset on anomalies in sensors simulation

description: MIDAS is a dataset of simulated runs of an ice cream factory with anomalies injected into its sensors. The IEEE DataPort page says the simulation has six modules (mixer, pasteuriser, homogeniser, ageing and cooling, dynamic freezer and hardening), and that analog level and temperature sensor values were altered with three anomaly types (frozen value, step change and ramp change) across 1,000 runs, 258 of them without anomalies, with the simulator code on GitHub. It was submitted by Tijana Markovic, Miguel Leon, Björn Leander and Sasikumar Punnekkat and last updated on 23 December 2022, as one CSV zip of about 2.16 GB. DataCite gives the licence as CC BY 4.0, but the page marks it a Standard Dataset, so the file needs an IEEE DataPort subscription (US$40 a month, free for IEEE Society members); the GitHub repository is openly readable. Coverage is one simulated food plant. Caveats: the author affiliation is not stated on the page read, and the data are simulated. For simulation it gives labelled sensor faults in a multi-stage food process to test anomaly detection and how a bad sensor spreads through a production line. Related catalogue records include IndPenSim and the Tennessee Eastman process anomaly detection data.
